messages:
elaine: @customer-a-team thanks for the report — we see your production app started getting 500s on KMS calls after the VPC maintenance window. Root error from our side: `kms client: dial tcp: i/o timeout` and the redwood-kms-agent logs show repeated TLS handshake timeouts. Can you share a quick repro and whether you use a proxy/NAT gateway?

customer-a-team: App stack: private deployment (VPC), kms-agent running on EC2 in private subnet, egress via NAT gateway + perimeter proxy. Symptoms: intermittent `500` for sign/decrypt, about ~30% of requests fail, others succeed. From the bastion I can sometimes `curl` the HSM endpoint but often it hangs. No config changed on our side during the window.

elaine: Ok — first checks: DNS resolution for the HSM endpoints, TCP connectivity, and TLS/SNI. Can you run `dig +short kms.hsm.provider.com` and `openssl s_client -connect kms.hsm.provider.com:443 -servername kms.hsm.provider.com` from the bastion and paste outputs? Also paste a short snippet of `/var/log/redwood-kms-agent.log` around a failure.

customer-a-team: Paste:
```
$ dig +short kms.hsm.provider.com
10.12.5.23
10.12.5.24

$ openssl s_client -connect 10.12.5.23:443
CONNECTED(00000003)
140356...0000:error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure:../ssl/record/rec_layer_s3.c:1543:SSL alert number 40
---
no peer certificate available
---
```
And kms-agent log: `time="2026-06-12T02:13:44Z" level=error msg="dial tcp 10.12.5.23:443: i/o timeout (tls handshake)"`

raj: Two things jump out:
- Dig returned private IPs (10.12.x.x) — is that a Route53 private zone override? Good to verify the target IPs didn't change during maintenance.
- Your `openssl` call used raw IP in the connect; the server likely expects SNI (hostname). `openssl s_client -connect 10.12.5.23:443 -servername kms.hsm.provider.com` would surface cert details. The failure `alert handshake failure` often means the server rejected the TLS because of SNI mismatch or ALPN/proxy inspection.

david: Also check whether the perimeter proxy or NAT is doing TLS intercept or re-writing SNI. We saw a similar issue where a firewall had an active TLS-inspection appliance that strips SNI when dest is an IP route. Quick checks: tcpdump for client hello SNI and `curl --resolve` test.

raj: From bastion run:
```
sudo tcpdump -n -s 0 -A 'host 10.12.5.23 and port 443' -c 50 > /tmp/tcpdump.out
openssl s_client -connect 10.12.5.23:443 -servername kms.hsm.provider.com -brief
```
And `curl -v --resolve kms.hsm.provider.com:443:10.12.5.23 https://kms.hsm.provider.com/health`

customer-a-team: tcpdump shows ClientHello with no SNI in many attempts. When I force `-servername` I get cert `*.hsm.provider.net` and valid chain. But the kms-agent appears to use IP in some threads (we use an IP cache in the agent). The agent config uses `dns_cache=true` and cached IPs; sometimes the agent dials IP without passing server_name. Agent log shows: `tls: no SNI passed`.

david: Aha — that's likely the cause. HSM requires SNI to route to the correct tenant cert. Our kms-agent must send SNI on all outbound TLS. Possible triggers: recent kernel glibc/resolver change or proxy rewriting. Two mitigation paths: 1) configure the agent to always use the hostname (disable direct-IP dialing / set `tls_server_name` in agent config), or 2) ensure your VPC DNS returns hostname and agent does TLS with `-servername`.

elaine: For immediate mitigation, try updating the agent config on one instance:
```
# /etc/redwood/kms-agent.yaml
endpoint: "kms.hsm.provider.com:443"
use_ip_direct: false
tls_server_name: "hsm.provider.net"
```
then `sudo systemctl restart redwood-kms-agent` and tail logs. Also add the HSM egress IPs into your firewall allowlist (NAT/proxy) and permit outbound 443 to 10.12.5.23/24.

customer-a-team: Did that on a canary host: after restart, logs show `tls handshake ok` and no errors for 15 minutes; app errors dropped to 0 on that canary.

raj: We should also update perimeter proxy to preserve SNI and not terminate TLS for that destination. Please open a ticket with the proxy team to disable inspection for `kms.hsm.provider.com` and confirm there's no middlebox rewriting SNI.

deploy-bot: noted deploy event 1769202845 - restarted redwood-kms-agent on i-0a1b2c3d (canary).

david: Long-term fix: we will push agent change to force SNI and avoid dialing cached IPs without `tls_server_name`. I'll open a PR to add `tls_server_name` fallback and a config toggle `force_sni=true`. Also add improved logging when SNI is absent.

elaine: For the support ticket we need the postmortem steps: reproduce (tcpdump + openssl with/without -servername), mitigation (set `use_ip_direct=false` + `tls_server_name` + add allowlist entries), and next actions (PR + proxy ticket + run a 24h canary). Can you confirm we have these in the ticket?

customer-a-team: Confirmed — I've opened support ticket #SUP-9921 with diagnostics and allowed IPs (10.12.5.23/24). Thanks, canary looks stable. :thumbsup:

elaine: Great — marking this thread as tracked in the support ticket. If anything regresses ping @raj and we'll escalate to network infra. :white_check_mark:
